topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Hidden Logic
target_audience: High school students or introductory computer science learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
lecture_lines: Binary uses only two: zero and one.
Think of bits as light switches.
animations: Create Text "Our world uses ten digits." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display digits 0-9 in a row at center-left.
Create Text "Binary uses only two: zero and one." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display bit '0' and '1' in blue (#3498DB) at center.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
lecture_lines: Smaller disks must stay above larger ones.
Move all disks to the final rod.
animations: Create Text "Three rods hold stacked disks." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display three disks in red (#E74C3C) on the first rod.
Create Text "Smaller disks must stay above larger ones." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show an invalid move attempt flashed in red (#E74C3C) and correct stacking in green (#2ECC71).
Create Text "Move all disks to the final rod." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Animate disks moving from start rod to final rod using a step-by-step path in purple (#9B59B6).

sections.title: The Binary Connection
lecture_lines: Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one.
Binary numbers reveal the next move.
Each bit corresponds to a specific disk.
animations: Create Text "Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display formula 2^{n}-1 using MathTex in white (#FFFFFF).
Create Text "Binary numbers reveal the next move." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display binary sequence 000 to 111 changing rhythmically below disks.
Create Text "Each bit corresponds to a specific disk." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Use color-coded arrows linking binary bits in blue (#3498DB) to specific disks.

sections.title: Visualizing the Algorithm
lecture_lines: Changing bits dictate each disk shift.
Small disks move frequently, large ones slowly.
animations: Create Text "Watch the binary rhythm unfold." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show a binary counter ticking up from 000 to 111.
Create Text "Changing bits dictate each disk shift." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Highlight the changing bit in gold (#F39C12) whenever a disk moves.
Create Text "Small disks move frequently, large ones slowly." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show smallest disk moving at high frequency and largest at low frequency.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Computers use this for memory management.
